Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:10:1.hebrew: כל משימות - מריבוייא דמשמעות דקרא קא יליף: מ״שום תשים״, ״מקרב אחיך תשים״ — כל משימות, ואפי' סנהדרי קטנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:10:1.english: All appointments - He derives [this] from the amplification in the verse's meaning: from "You shall surely set" [and] "from among your brothers you shall set" — all appointments, and even [to] a Minor Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:11:1.hebrew: במילי דשמיא - בגבאי צדקה, ובקיצותה וחלוקתה, וסדר מתורגמנין ומפטירין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:11:1.english: In matters of Heaven - In [overseeing] the charity collectors, and its assessment and its distribution, and the order of the translators and the readers of the haftarah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:11:2.hebrew: במילי דמתא - שאר צרכי צבור לדברי הרשות — לטורזינא, לכריא פתיא, לאגלי גפא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:11:2.english: In the matters of the city - The rest of the communal needs for secular matters — [such as] for weapons [for the watch], for digging [public] drinking wells, [and] for [locking] the city gates.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:11:3.hebrew: לאשרי - כמו לתור להם מנוחה (במדבר י׳:ל״ג), שתרגומו: אתר בית משרי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:11:3.english: Let him host - Like "to seek out a resting place for them" (Numbers 10:33), [which the Targum renders as] "a place of lodging."

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:12:1.english: Would deal with them - He would concern himself with them, to honor them and install them in [positions of] authority.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:12:2.hebrew: ריש כורי - ממונה על המדות, לשון לתך וכור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:12:2.english: An officer of kor measures - An appointee over measures, an expression [related to] letekh and kor.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:12:3.hebrew: גרגותא - להשקות בית השלחין. פעמים שהם של רבים, וממנים שוטר עליו שלא ישקה איש ביומו של חבירו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:12:3.english: Irrigation - [A ditch used] to irrigate an irrigated field. Sometimes they belong to many [people], and they appoint an officer over it so that a person will not irrigate on his fellow's day.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:14:1.hebrew: בחיילות של בית דוד - שהיו באים בחלוקה, חדש בחדש, וחוזרין חלילה, והוא לשון איסטרטיא. וכותבין בשמות: משפחת פלוני ופלוני בחדש פלוני. והיו זהירין לייחסן מכל מום, כדמפרש — שתסייעם זכות אבותם במלחמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:14:1.english: In the military troops of the House of David - For they would come in divisions, month by month, and cycle through in turn; and this is the meaning of [the term] istratya. And they would record [them] by name: The family of So-and-so and So-and-so in such-and-such month. And they were careful to trace their lineage [to be free] from any blemish, as [the Gemara] explains: so that the merit of their ancestors would assist them in war.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:14:2.english: And is there no more? - We do not read [this].

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:15:1.english: Zelek the Ammonite - He is counted among the chief mighty men who belonged to David.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:15:2.hebrew: דאתי מעמון - ונתגייר, אלמא לא הקפיד על הגרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:15:2.english: That he came from Ammon - And converted; evidently, [David] was not particular about converts.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:16:1.hebrew: והא אמר רב נחמן - במס' עבודה זרה (דף מד.): בא אתי הגיתי, שהיה עובד כוכבים, ובטלה לעבודת כוכבים של עטרת מלכם — והוא שם שיקוץ עמונים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:16:1.english: But didn’t Rav Naḥman say - In Tractate Avodah Zarah (daf 44a): Ittai the Gittite, who was a gentile, came and nullified the idol of the crown of Malcam — and this is the name of the abomination of the Ammonites.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:17:1.hebrew: ילדים - בחורים היו לדוד בחיילותיו, ולא היו בניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:17:1.english: Youths - They were young men in David's army, and they were not his sons.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:17:2.hebrew: בני יפת תואר - נשים שלקחו אנשי ישראל במלחמה, כדכתיב (דברים כ״א:י״ב): "והבאתה אל תוך ביתך", ומתוך כך היו נוהגים כמשפטי העובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:17:2.english: Sons of a beautiful woman - [Sons of] women whom the men of Israel took in war, as it is written: “And you shall bring her into your house” (Deuteronomy 21:12); and because of this, they would conduct themselves according to the customs of the idolaters.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:17:3.english: Cutting [their hair in the] komei [style] and growing a belorit - [They grew it] at the back of their neck.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:17:4.english: To frighten the world - But they would not go down into the midst of the battle with Israel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:1:1.hebrew: מוקי לה בלוייה וישראלית - כדקתני מתניתין: ״מוסיפין עליהן עוד אחת״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:1:1.english: He interprets it [as referring to] a Levite woman and an Israelite woman - As the Mishnah teaches: "They add to them one more."

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:1:2.english: Shall we say it disagrees - With our Mishnah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:1:3.hebrew: מאי מוסיפין עוד אחת - דקתני מתני':
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:1:3.english: What is [the meaning of] “they add one more”? - [This refers to] that which the Mishnah teaches.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:2:1.hebrew: זו דברי ר"מ - סתם מתניתין דמצריך בדיקה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:2:1.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir - [This refers to] the anonymous Mishnah, which requires an investigation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:2:2.hebrew: כשקרא עליו ערער - א"צ בדיקה אלא אם קראו עליה שני עדים שמץ של פסול, ולא שמעידים עדות גמורה, אלא יציאת קול. וכיון דקרא עליה ערער, אמאי פליגי רבנן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:2:2.english: When an objection was raised against it - [An investigation] is not required unless two witnesses raised a taint of disqualification against it — and not that they testify with full testimony, but rather [to] the emergence of a rumor. And since an objection was raised against it, why would the Rabbis disagree?

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:2:3.english: The one who taught this - In the name of Rav.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:2:4.english: Did not teach that - And Rav Yehuda and Rav Ḥama are [differing] Amora'im according to [the opinion of] Rav.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:3:1.english: He must investigate her - Even according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:4:1.hebrew: ששם היו יושבים - בלשכת הגזית היו יושבים סנהדרין, מתמיד של שחר עד תמיד של בין הערבים, ומייחסים את הכהנים והלויים, להבדיל פסולים מן העבודה ומן הדוכן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:4:1.english: For there they would sit - In the Chamber of Hewn Stone the Sanhedrin would sit, from the morning daily offering until the afternoon daily offering, and verify the lineage of the priests and the Levites, to separate those who were disqualified from the service and from the platform.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:5:1.hebrew: מכל מום - פסול יוחסין. ובסנהדרין קאמר — או גדולה או קטנה — אבל דיינין בעלמא לא, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:5:1.english: Of any blemish - Flawed lineage. And it is speaking of a Sanhedrin — whether the Great [Sanhedrin] or the Small [Sanhedrin] — but ordinary judges, no, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:6:1.english: With you - Of [unflawed] lineage like you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:7:1.hebrew: ודלמא משום שכינה - סנהדרין שבאותה שעה הוצרכו להיות מיוחסין משום שכינה; על שם נבואה נאספו שם, כדכתיב (במדבר י״א:י״ז): ״ואצלתי מן הרוח״ וגו'. אבל סנהדרין שהן לדון, כגון סנהדרי דיתרו חותן משה — לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:7:1.english: And perhaps [it was] on account of the Divine Presence - The Sanhedrin of that time was required to be of [unflawed] lineage on account of the Divine Presence; for they were assembled there for the purpose of prophecy, as it is written (Numbers 11:17): “And I will take of the spirit...” etc. But a Sanhedrin that is [appointed] to judge, such as the courts of Jethro, father-in-law of Moses — [was] not.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:7:2.hebrew: ונשאו אתך - גרסינן, ולא גרס "במשא העם", אלא אסנהדרין דיתרו קאי: "והקל מעליך ונשאו אתך":
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:7:2.english: “And they shall bear with you” - This is our reading, and one does not read “in the burden of the people”; rather, [the verse] refers to the Sanhedrin of Yitro: “So shall they make it easier for you, and they shall bear with you.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:8:1.hebrew: שוטרי הרבים - דיינין בעלמא, שאינן ממנין עשרים ושלש של סנהדרי קטנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:8:1.english: Public officers - Ordinary judges, who are not of the count of twenty-three of a Minor Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:8:2.english: In Jerusalem - They were particular about all their judges, to verify their lineage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:9:1.hebrew: ממשכנין - נוטלי' משכונות על צדקה שיפסקו עליו, ואינו נותנן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:9:1.english: They take collateral - They take collateral for charity that they assessed upon him, and he does not give it:

Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:9:2.hebrew: ואפי' בערב שבת - שהאדם טרוד, ומתוך כך מריבין עמהן ומבזין אותן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 76b:9:2.english: And even on the eve of Shabbat - For a person is preoccupied, and because of this, they quarrel with them and insult them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 76b:4:1.hebrew: אין בודקין מן המזבח ולמעלה כו' - ואם תאמר: אמאי לא קתני "אין בודקין משטרות ולמעלה", דהא אמרינן בפ"ב דכתובות (דף כד:) מעלים משטרות ליוחסין? וי"ל: דאין זה רבותא, דהא עדות מעליא הוא. וא"ת: ניתני נמי "אין בודקין מנשיאות כפים ולמעלה ומתרומה ולמעלה", כדאמר בפרק ב' דכתובות (שם) מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין? ויש לומר: דגם זה אינו רבותא, כיון דלא שייך אלא בכהנים. אבל הא [דתנן] "אין בודקין מן המזבח ולמעלה" — רבותא הוא, דמיירי אפילו בעבודות הכשרות בזרים, כגון שחיטה או הפשט; אע"ג דשחיטה כשרה בנשים ובעבדים — היינו דיעבד, אבל לכתחילה לא עבדי כי אם כשרים מיוחסין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 76b:4:1.english: "One does not investigate from the altar and above, etc." - And if you say: Why does [the mishna] not teach, "One does not investigate from [signatures on] legal deeds and above," for we say in the second chapter of Ketubot (24b): "One elevates from deeds to lineage"? And one can say: That is not a novelty, for that is superior testimony. And if you say: Let it also teach, "One does not investigate from the raising of hands [the Priestly Blessing] and above, and from terumah and above," as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Ketubot (ibid.): "One elevates from terumah to lineage"? And one can say: This too is not a novelty, since it applies only to priests. However, that which [the mishna taught], "One does not investigate from the altar and above," is a novelty, because it deals even with services that are valid [when performed] by non-priests, such as slaughtering or flaying; and even though slaughtering is valid [even when performed] by women and slaves, that is [only] after the fact [bedi'avad], but ab initio [lekhatḥilah] only fit individuals of [verified] lineage would perform [them].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 76b:7:1.hebrew: והקל מעליך ונשאו אתך - ה"ג רש"י, ול"ג "במשא העם" — שהרי גבי שכינה כתיב כן, והאי קרא דהכא כתיב ביתרו, ולא כתיב ביה "במשא העם":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 76b:7:1.english: "So shall they make it easier for you and bear [the burden] with you" - Thus Rashi reads, and he does not read "in the burden of the people," for that is written with regard to the Divine Presence, and this verse here is written in [the passage of] Jethro, and "in the burden of the people" is not written in it.
